A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 25-page versions of the same SPDIM work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1-A.7 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original simulations and EEG motor-imagery and sleep-staging experiments in Section 4, Figures 2-3, and the main and appendix result tables.

after.justification: v5 retains these original simulation and EEG experimental results, including the detailed results and sensitivity analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The SPDIM bias and geodesic variants, decoding architecture, information-maximization objective and adaptation procedure in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulations, four motor-imagery datasets and four sleep-staging datasets. Cross-session, cross-subject and label-shift scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment, including RCT in simulations and EA, STMA, SPDDSBN, IM variants and neural-network baselines in the EEG comparisons.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, balanced-accuracy metrics, training budgets and splits are identical. Both retain leave-one-group-out motor-imagery evaluation and 10-fold grouped sleep-staging evaluation.

E4.justification: The sleep-staging ablations in Tables 2 and A3 and simulation sensitivity analyses in Figures 2 and A1-A4 are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both retain the same standard-deviation reporting, Figure 3 confidence intervals and permutation-paired t-tests with t-max correction. Seed and repeated-run disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports the same SPDIM overall balanced accuracies of 73.5% for healthy subjects and 69.9% for patients.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations and Propositions 1-2 are unchanged, including their proofs in Appendices A.1-A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same claims about the generative model, alignment under distribution shifts, SPDIM's contribution and its empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Both retain the limitation that noise and outliers can produce inappropriate bias estimates and increased performance variability.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.6-A.7 retain identical software, hardware, preprocessing, architecture and optimization details. Code and data access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and positioning relative to prior Riemannian alignment and source-free adaptation research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint. Under review.' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated and gains a link to v5; body wording and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3 and A1-A4 and Tables 1-2 and A1-A5 retain their structure, captions, graphics and placement. The header/stamp text updates do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v5 updates publication status and arXiv metadata while retaining the same scientific text, evidence, proofs, limitations and implementation details throughout the appendices. These administrative updates do not meaningfully change the paper's rigor, clarity or reproducibility.
